fleetcheck

fleetcheck measures how closely the fleet mean-field model reproduces the malariasimulation individual-based model (IBM) of P. falciparum and P. vivax malaria.

It is a twin-fidelity check: it measures agreement between two models, not agreement with data. fleet inherits its epidemiological standing from the IBM only as far as the gap measured here is small relative to the IBM’s own uncertainty, and a faithful reproduction of the IBM reproduces its biases too. Nothing here is validation against observation.

Claims register

Each claim fleet makes about agreeing with the IBM is recorded in claims.yml with the criterion that decides it, the value measured against that criterion, and a verdict.

P. falciparum

12 claims: 0 failing, 0 untested, 0 open, 12 pass.

  1. pass prevalence-eir: LM prevalence in 2-10 year olds tracks the IBM across transmission intensity.
  2. pass clinical-allage-eir: All-age clinical incidence tracks the IBM across transmission intensity.
  3. pass clinical-under5-eir: Under-5 clinical incidence tracks the IBM across transmission intensity.
  4. pass severe-allage-eir: All-age severe incidence tracks the IBM across transmission intensity.
  5. pass age-profile-clinical: The age distribution of clinical incidence tracks the IBM.
  6. pass age-profile-severe: The age distribution of severe incidence tracks the IBM.
  7. pass intervention-impact: The modelled impact of each intervention matches the IBM.
  8. pass real-settings-correlation: Agreement holds across real transmission settings, not just synthetic scenarios.
  9. pass parameter-draws: The change a posterior parameter draw makes to prevalence, clinical and severe incidence matches the IBM’s.
  10. pass population-age-structure: The population age structure matches the IBM’s.
  11. pass speed: fleet is fast enough to be worth using in place of the IBM.
  12. pass seed-stability: An undisturbed run holds the equilibrium it was seeded at.

P. vivax

10 claims: 2 failing, 0 untested, 0 open, 8 pass.

  1. pass prevalence-eir-pv: LM prevalence in 2-10 year olds tracks the IBM across transmission intensity.
  2. pass clinical-allage-eir-pv: All-age clinical incidence tracks the IBM across transmission intensity.
  3. pass clinical-under5-eir-pv: Under-5 clinical incidence tracks the IBM across transmission intensity.
  4. pass relapse-allage-eir-pv: All-age relapse incidence tracks the IBM across transmission intensity.
  5. pass hypnozoite-carriage-eir-pv: The share of people carrying hypnozoites tracks the IBM across transmission intensity.
  6. pass age-profile-clinical-pv: The age distribution of clinical incidence tracks the IBM.
  7. FAIL intervention-impact-pv: The modelled impact of each intervention, radical cure included, matches the IBM.
  8. pass population-age-structure-pv: The population age structure matches the IBM’s.
  9. FAIL speed-pv: fleet is fast enough to be worth using in place of the IBM.
  10. pass seed-stability-pv: An undisturbed run settles to a steady state, off the equilibrium it was seeded at, as the IBM’s does.

The criterion, measured value and figure for each claim are on the evidence pages for P. falciparum and P. vivax.

The claims ask whether fleet tracks the IBM: shape, direction, and agreement within the IBM’s own stochastic spread. A mean-field model and an individual-based model sit a few per cent apart for structural reasons; where that matters, it is noted against the claim it affects.

The list above is generated from claims.yml by report/make_scoreboard.R.

Installation

fleetcheck is not on CRAN. It is used from a clone of the repository:

git clone https://github.com/pwinskill/fleetcheck.git
cd fleetcheck

Reading and checking the register needs only:

install.packages(c("yaml", "pkgload", "devtools"))

Re-running the models also needs fleet, malariasimulation and the output post-processor postie. fleet compiles C++ and installs dust2, monty and malariaEquilibrium with it.

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("pwinskill/fleet")
remotes::install_github("mrc-ide/malariasimulation")
remotes::install_github("mrc-ide/postie")
remotes::install_deps(dependencies = TRUE)

Usage

From the repository root, read the register as text or as a data frame, without running any model:

pkgload::load_all()
writeLines(scoreboard())
subset(read_claims(), status != "pass")

CI runs the unit tests, which include static checks of the validation scripts, and checks that the rendered copies of the register match claims.yml and that no claim has regressed. This takes seconds:

Rscript -e 'devtools::test()'
Rscript report/make_scoreboard.R --check
Rscript -e 'pkgload::load_all(quiet = TRUE); check_claims()'

check_claims() fails on any failing claim not listed in its allow_fail argument, and an allow_fail entry whose claim has no explanatory note is itself an error.

After a change to fleet, re-run fleet alone against the committed IBM results. This takes minutes and is the check to run most often:

Rscript validations/02-scenarios/assess.R

Methods describes how claims are decided, and how to re-run each body of evidence, redraw the figures and update the register.

At a glance

  • A twin-fidelity check: agreement between two models, not validation against data. Each claim records the criterion that decides it and the cost of reproducing it, from seconds to about two hours on ten cores.
